title: Review of Financial Information
outcomes: Perform reviews of historical statements under SRE 2400.
Review interim financial information under SRE 2410.
Apply enquiry and analytical review procedures.

meta.exam_tip: Use negative-form wording in review conclusions.

concepts.title: Review engagements on historical statements (SRE 2400)
body: A review of historical financial statements (SRE 2400) gives limited assurance, worded negatively: the practitioner says they found no reason to think the statements depart from the framework.
Procedures are primarily enquiry and analytical procedures, designed to reduce engagement risk to a level acceptable for limited assurance — much less work than an audit.
The practitioner must comply with ethics, apply professional skepticism and judgement, and perform additional procedures if matters suggest material misstatement.
concepts.analogy: Reviews give limited assurance through enquiry and analytics.
concepts.work: A small company's lender may accept reviewed rather than audited statements.

concepts.title: Review of interim financial information by the entity's auditor (SRE 2410)
body: SRE 2410 applies when the entity's own auditor reviews interim financial information (e.g. quarterly results of listed companies under SEBI LODR). The auditor's knowledge from the annual audit helps focus enquiries.
The auditor updates understanding of the entity and internal control, reads minutes, considers prior misstatements, and checks that interim information agrees with records.
Written representations are obtained; matters found are communicated to management and TCWG, including possible fraud or non-compliance.
concepts.analogy: The annual auditor reviews quarterly results using what they already know.
concepts.work: A listed company's auditor issues a limited review report on quarterly results.

concepts.title: Review procedures: enquiry and analytics
body: Review procedures: enquiries of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters (on recording, changes in policies, unusual transactions, subsequent events, going concern, fraud and non-compliance), analytical procedures (comparisons with prior periods, budgets, expected relationships), and reading the information for consistency.
If something suggests material misstatement, the practitioner performs additional procedures sufficient to conclude.
Procedures are not designed to test controls or obtain corroborating evidence as in an audit.
concepts.analogy: Ask the right people and compare the right numbers.
concepts.work: A sudden margin jump triggers follow-up enquiries.

concepts.title: Review conclusions and reports
body: Conclusions: unmodified (negative assurance), qualified (material but not pervasive misstatement or limitation), adverse (material and pervasive misstatement) and disclaimer (material and pervasive limitation).

The report identifies the information reviewed, responsibilities of management and the practitioner, explains that a review covers far less ground than an audit so no audit opinion is given, and gives the conclusion.
If management refuses to correct misstatements, the practitioner communicates with TCWG and may need to consider withdrawal or modification.
concepts.analogy: Review conclusions mirror audit opinions but in negative form.
concepts.work: A report says: "nothing has come to our attention..." for an unmodified conclusion.

illustrations.title: An unexplained margin jump
illustrations.q: While reviewing a listed company's quarterly results, the auditor notes gross profit of ₹45 crore on revenue of ₹110 crore this quarter, against ₹30 crore on ₹100 crore in earlier quarters, with no change in prices or product mix. What should the auditor do?

head: Step
Working / Action
Result
rows: Ask management to explain the jump (cut-off, inventory valuation, cost allocation)
If explanations are unsatisfactory, perform further procedures
If misstatement is confirmed and uncorrected, modify the conclusion
solution.title: SRE 2410 analytics

illustrations.title: Choosing the review conclusion
illustrations.q: In a review: (a) nothing has come to attention suggesting misstatement; (b) a material, non-pervasive misstatement exists; (c) a misstatement is material and pervasive; (d) management imposes a pervasive scope limitation. Give the conclusion in each.

jobs.title: Quarterly limited review
jobs.situation: A listed client's Q2 results are due in 10 days.
steps: Obtain representations and draft the review report.
jobs.takeaway: Analytics plus sharp enquiries drive a good review.

mcqs.explain: Negative form. In practice: less than audit.

mcqs.q: Review of interim information by the entity's auditor is governed by:
mcqs.explain: Entity's auditor. In practice: quarterly results.

mcqs.explain: Limited scope. In practice: follow up anomalies.

mcqs.q: A material and pervasive misstatement in a review leads to:
mcqs.explain: Mirrors SA 705. In practice: describe basis.

mcqs.q: The review report states that a review is:
options: Substantially less in scope than an audit
mcqs.explain: Clarifies limits. In practice: no audit opinion.

mcqs.q: If enquiries suggest material misstatement, the practitioner should:
mcqs.explain: Sufficient to conclude. In practice: document.

mcqs.q: A pervasive scope limitation imposed by management leads to:
mcqs.explain: Cannot conclude. In practice: communicate to TCWG.
Supports review. In practice: dated with report.

summary: SRE 2400 other practitioners; SRE 2410 entity's auditor.
remember: Review is much less than an audit.

viva.q: What assurance does a review give?
viva.model: Limited assurance, expressed in negative form that nothing has come to attention suggesting the statements are misstated.

viva.q: Why is SRE 2410 different from SRE 2400?
viva.model: SRE 2410 is performed by the entity's own auditor, who uses knowledge from the annual audit; SRE 2400 is for other practitioners.
Recording of transactions, changes in policies, unusual transactions, subsequent events, going concern and fraud or non-compliance.

viva.q: What forms can a review conclusion take?
viva.model: Unmodified, qualified, adverse or a disclaimer of conclusion.

viva.q: What if management refuses to correct a misstatement found in a review?
viva.model: Communicate with those charged with governance, modify the conclusion, and consider withdrawal if needed.

cases.title: Track Analytics Ltd.
cases.case: The statutory auditor of Track Analytics, a listed company, reviews its Q3 results. Management has not recognised an impairment the auditor estimates at ₹12 crore (materiality ₹8 crore), confined to one asset. Management also declines to provide access to board minutes for the quarter.

mcqs.explain: Entity's auditor reviewing interim results. In practice: SEBI LODR.
mcqs.topic: Review of interim financial information by the entity's auditor (SRE 2410)

mcqs.q: The unrecognised impairment alone leads to:
mcqs.explain: Material, confined to one item. In practice: quantify.

mcqs.q: Refusal of access to minutes is:
options: A scope limitation to discuss with TCWG
mcqs.explain: May lead to modified conclusion. In practice: assess pervasiveness.

mcqs.q: The main procedures for this review are:
mcqs.explain: Limited scope. In practice: plus representations.
